precepts.text: But there rose up certain of the sect of the Pharisees which believed, saying, That it was needful to circumcise them, and to command them to keep the law of Moses. That is the history it goes back to.
precepts.point: When Deacon mentioned the circumcision, that goes back to the history in Acts chapter 15, meaning the Pharisees were pushing first and foremost that they had to circumcise after the manner of Moses, meaning the old covenant of animal sacrifice, and not Christ. So not just circumcision meaning your foreskin, because that is a law that we have to do, but they pushed that before they pushed Christ.
precepts.why:
John is the only one in the Bible who calls a system or a person the antichrist. The prophets spoke of that last kingdom that would fight against Christ at his return, but they did not call it antichrist. John says “as ye have heard that antichrist shall come”, which is future, “even now are there many antichrists”. Anti means against. Even in John's time many were against Christ.

“They went out from us, but they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would no doubt have continued with us”. These were men among the apostles who up and left the apostles and their teachings, which were the teachings of Christ, and went out teaching against them. They said the resurrection had taken place already. They taught that you have to be circumcised. That is an antichrist doctrine, one form of antichrist in the time of the apostles.

That goes back to the history in Acts 15: “But there rose up certain of the sect of the Pharisees which believed, saying, That it was needful to circumcise them, and to command them to keep the law of Moses.” The Pharisees were pushing first and foremost that they had to be circumcised after the manner of Moses, meaning the old covenant of animal sacrifice, and not Christ. It is not only circumcision of the foreskin, because that is a law we have to do; it is that they pushed that before they pushed Christ.

So from the beginning there were many antichrists: those who went out from the apostles and taught contrary to Christ. That is why John says “they went out, that they might be made manifest that they were not all of us.”

precepts.text: These be they who separate themselves, sensual, having not the Spirit. So there are going to be those that separate themselves. Sensual, having not the spirit of the Lord. How can we prove that? What does the Lord require us to do on the holy Sabbath day? So when the spirit rises up in you to stay at home, or to play Sabbath sick, or to forsake the assembling of ourselves together, whose spirit are you moving in? The Lord is about unity. The Lord has never been about separation. So when that spirit rises up in you, you have to be able to recognise it and then force yourself past that point. Because do you wake up every day on the right side of the bed? Do you wake up and everything is perfect? But you have to push past it. You do not call off work every day. You still go to work, you still shuffle the white man's papers and stand by the coffee machine and act interested in the job, but you do not really want to be there, and you still go. The hope is that once we are among each other, someone who has the spirit of the Lord can be so infectious that it can jump on me and I can get in the spirit of the Lord.
precepts.point: So the seduction is always going to be there. At various times it was Christ did not exist, or Christ did not die on the cross, or Christ did not rise from the dead, or now Christ is a white man, when there is not one scriptural proof to back it up. Why? Because Satan's spirit worketh in the children of disobedience. God gave commandments. You learn the commandments. And then you say, we can eat whatever we want, we can worship the Lord on Sunday, we do not have to keep the Sabbath day holy. You have now become disobedient, because God gave clear instructions on what we are commanded to do.
precepts.why:
John writes “concerning them that seduce you”, and verse 27 shows how the seduction comes: “ye need not that any man teach you”. The antichrist is going to try to teach you something. He isn't floating in the air going boo; he's teaching. What do you think all these apologetics are? That is the spirit of antichrist. Does that mean the bishops and deacons can't teach us? No. It is the ones who fell away: “They went out from us, but they were not of us”, and now all of a sudden they want to teach you.

Jude shows who they are: “These be they who separate themselves, sensual, having not the Spirit.” There will be those who separate themselves, sensual, not having the spirit of the Lord. How can we prove it? What does the Lord require of us on the holy Sabbath day? So when the spirit rises up in you to stay at home, to play Sabbath sick, to forsake the assembling of ourselves together, whose spirit are you moving in? You see how simple that is. The Lord is about unity; he has never been about separation.

When that spirit rises up in you, recognize it, say Satan is trying to get me, and force yourself past that point. Do you wake up every day on the right side of the bed, everything perfect? No, but you push past it. You don't call off work every day. You still go shuffle the white man's papers, stand by the coffee machine and the water cooler and act interested in the job when you don't want to be there. The hope is that once we are among each other, someone who has the spirit of the Lord can be so infectious that it jumps on me, and I get in the spirit of the Lord.

The gripes and unresolved issues, hatred and jealousy, are what Satan uses as a reason to send you back to Caesar Borgia: he spoke rough to me, he didn't say anything to me. Some brothers and sisters, no matter what you do, you can't make them happy; some are ordained to be that sensual brother or sister. That is why we have to stay in the spirit.

precepts.text: The way: he that saith he abideth in him ought himself also so to walk, even as he walked.
precepts.point: I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.

note.label: Daily Bread for a Dying Man

precepts.why:
Christ says, “I am the way, the truth, and the life.” This goes into the bread of life: everything that happened with the manna was always symbolic of Christ, a shadow foreshadowing him. And the first thing he calls himself is the way.

John tells us what it means for Christ to be the way: “He that saith he abideth in him ought himself also so to walk, even as he walked.” We have to walk as he walked.

Christ is not a way you only talk about or feel; he is a path you walk. Whoever says he abides in Christ has to walk the same way Christ walked, in the same commandments, day by day. That is what it means to feed on him as the bread from heaven: to take in his word every day and live the way he lived.

precepts.text: He is the propitiation for our sins: and not for ours only, but also for the sins of the whole world. That world is scattered Israel, all Israel, that they might have time to repent.
precepts.point: The day of atonement: on the tenth day of the seventh month ye shall afflict your souls. Christ was that atonement.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
John says it plainly: “And he is the propitiation for our sins”. Christ is the atonement for our sins, the fulfilment of the day of atonement in Leviticus 23:27.

Then: “and not for ours only, but also for the sins of the whole world.” That world is the scattered Israelites, all Israel, so that they may have time to repent. It is talking about Israel; it is not talking about all nations.

The next reading shows it: in the high priest’s long garment “was the whole world”, and that world was the twelve tribes. So when Christ atones for the world, he atones for Israel wherever they have been scattered.

precepts.text: The beginning of pride is when one departeth from God and his heart is turned away from his maker: that is the pride of life.
precepts.point: Brothers, a sister in pants should infuriate you, not catch your eye; the Lord of Israel is the belt doing the whipping now, and it will continue as long as our people love this kingdom.
precepts.why:
John says “all that is in the world, the lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, is not of the Father, but is of the world.” The lust of the flesh: in America everything is accessible; order it and it's there in twenty minutes. The lust of the eyes: social media, looking at the big butt, keeping up with the Joneses, twerking, the competition of niggardom: I can jump on a car better than she can, I can roll a blunt this big, I can rap about nothing and can't say my ABCs. Our people love the world for those things but fail to love God.

And what is the pride of life? Sirach answers: “The beginning of pride is when one departeth from God, and his heart is turned away from his Maker.” That is the pride of life we just read in 1 John. It is when you hate God and retract yourself from the love of the heavenly Father, when you prefer this world, this system and this setup over the guidelines of God, and would rather have this phobia of freedom and be guided by your oppressors.

The scriptures say pride goeth before destruction. When you go contrary to the Lord, death is at your door: “For pride is the beginning of sin, and he that hath it shall pour out abomination: and therefore the Lord brought upon them strange calamities, and overthrew them utterly.”

Your heart is then removed from the one that created you. “And the world passeth away, and the lust thereof”: Esau's rulership is already ordained to pass away. Will you escape when the destruction comes, or pass away with it?

precepts.text: He that doeth the will of God is the one who delights in his law.
precepts.point: Brothers, a sister in pants should infuriate you, not catch your eye; the Lord of Israel is the belt doing the whipping now, and it will continue as long as our people love this kingdom.
precepts.why:
John says “the world passeth away, and the lust thereof: but he that doeth the will of God abideth for ever.” Who is he that doeth the will of God? David shows it: “I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart.” He that doeth the will of God is the one who delights in his law.

That one abides for ever: you will have everlasting life, and you are going to rule over these kingdoms. Everything you could not see yourself living without in this world shall come to an end, but the one with God's law in his heart abides.

So you must hate this world and everything in it. Brothers, you have to hate even the sight of a sister in pants, to the point where it infuriates you instead of catching your eye. The YNs, the young nuisances walking around in the community, should infuriate you. Bring back the belt. But we have a belt: the God of Israel, and he is doing the whipping right now, and it will continue as long as our people love this kingdom in captivity.

Love not the world. Delight in his law, do his will, and abide for ever.

precepts.text: Love not the world, neither the things that are in the world; if any man love the world, the love of the Father is not in him. America is the kingdom of sin, specifically designed against us to cater to and test the flesh, to forge you or destroy you; only the spiritually, mentally, and physically strong survive it. Scrolling is idle, porn, Instagram models, and clubbing are love of the world. All that is in the world, the lust of the flesh, the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, is not of the Father; Satan was given power over this world to get you operating outside your purpose.
precepts.point: Meats for the belly, and the belly for meats, but God shall destroy both it and them: you are arguing over food that God will destroy along with the one consuming it. Now the body is not for fornication, but for the Lord, and the Lord for the body. He moves from food to fornication, the man with his father's wife from the previous chapter, because both are self-control over your vessel, created to be used for the master's work.

note.label: Power Under Control: Food, Sex & Self-Mastery

precepts.why:
“All things are lawful unto me, but all things are not expedient: all things are lawful for me, but I will not be brought under the power of any.” John shows the power we must not come under: “Love not the world, neither the things that are in the world. If any man love the world, the love of the Father is not in him.”

The world here is predominantly America. America is the kingdom of sin, specifically designed and created against us, in complete opposition to us, to cater to and test the flesh. It is either to make you or break you, to forge you or destroy you. Only the strong, spiritually, mentally and physically, are going to survive this kingdom.

Do not love the things catered to us in entertainment, catered to us when we are bored and idle. Scrolling is idle; that is love of the world. Porn is love of the world. Instagram models are love of the world. Clubbing is love of the world.

“For all that is in the world, the lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, is not of the Father, but is of the world.” Satan was given power over this world, and he is going to try to get you to operate outside of your purpose. What looks good to the eyes and caters to the appetite is not always good; look past the outside to the ingredients. The body is not for any of that; it is for the Lord, and the Lord for the body.

precepts.text: The way of an adulterous woman: she eateth, and wipeth her mouth, and saith, I have done no wickedness. The song's line about loving an eater is this same characteristic.
precepts.point: Sisters should not be doing dances they see online. The 'eating' motion in the popular challenge is not about food, and the deacon takes the class to Proverbs to show what it actually describes.
precepts.why:
“Love not the world, neither the things that are in the world.” If you love this place, the love of the Father is not in you. The state of mind of a saint is, I want to be up out of here; I hate this place. All that is in the world is “the lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life”, and the lust of the eyes today is TikTok and social media, where the minds of a lot of young brothers and sisters are.

There is a challenge everybody is doing, a dance where they act like they are eating something. The song is called feeling on my body, and it is all about sex. Young brothers and sisters, even among us, watch it and mimic it, and some school sisters were doing that dumb, stupid dance on the new moon. When she says she loves an eater, you think she is talking about eating food? She ain't talking about eating food. She's talking about eating sausage.

The scripture shows what it is: “Such is the way of an adulterous woman; she eateth, and wipeth her mouth, and saith, I have done no wickedness.” She eats and wipes her mouth, and then says she has done no wickedness. That is the characteristic of an adulterous, wicked woman, and that is what the dance is about: sucking rod.

So sisters, you should not be doing those dances. You don't even understand what's behind them. It is the lust of the eyes: you see it on social media and think it's cool. It isn't innocent; you are conjuring demons. We are supposed to be separate, not following the things we see in the world, because the world passeth away, and the lust thereof, “but he that doeth the will of God abideth for ever.”

precepts.text: They went out from us, but they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would no doubt have continued with us. This is a hospital; those who leave over an offence were never of us.
precepts.point: If a spouse who does not believe is pleased to dwell with you, they stay because they love you. When a spouse gets up and leaves because you came to the truth, that person never really loved you.
precepts.why:
Paul says, “we are bound to give thanks alway to God for you, brethren beloved of the Lord, because God hath from the beginning chosen you to salvation.” Which of you gives thanks to God every day for the brother or sister sitting next to you? That is the spirit we have to war with from now on: no evil thought of a brother or a sister, but praying and fasting for them, so we may be found faithful in the eyes of God. And it is not a coincidence you are in here. The salvation you are receiving was given to you from the beginning.

How do we know? “They went out from us, but they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would no doubt have continued with us.” Some brothers and sisters will come among us who are not of us. If they had been, then no matter what we went through, they would still be with us.

In this body we are going to go through things. This is a hospital; we all need medicine, and the word of God is what heals us. A sister said she left because another sister offended her. How many times have we offended the Lord? We have to build our spirit up so we do not move over every little stupidity.

“But they went out, that they might be made manifest that they were not all of us.” They were not the chosen. The same goes for a spouse: if the unbelieving spouse is pleased to dwell with you, they stay because they love you. When a wife or husband gets up and leaves because you came to the truth, that person never really loved you. So you who are still here, it is no coincidence: you were chosen from the beginning.

precepts.text: If a man say, I love God, and hateth his brother, he is a liar. He who loveth God loveth his brother also. What the white man calls patriotism among his people we must practise among ours: God and race.
precepts.point: He that loveth his brother abideth in the light and there is none occasion of stumbling in him; he that hateth his brother walketh in darkness, because that darkness hath blinded his eyes. Hate of your brother blinds you to deep but basic scriptures.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
John says it again in his fourth chapter: “If a man say, I love God, and hateth his brother, he is a liar: for he that loveth not his brother whom he hath seen, how can he love God whom he hath not seen?” And: “this commandment have we from him, That he who loveth God love his brother also.”

You can't love one and hate the other. It is impossible. If you love your brother, by default you love God; if you love God, by default you love your brother. They go hand in hand: God and people, God and race. What the white man promotes among his people is what we should promote among ourselves. When we say it, we're called racist; when they say it, they're patriots.

That is the light and darkness of 1 John 2. “He that saith he is in the light, and hateth his brother, is in darkness even until now.” Picture our people in captivity, while the ones who enslaved us rule. For hundreds of years they spent billions, even trillions, to hide our history from us. They tortured us, beat us, raped us, castrated us, and broke us physically, mentally, psychologically and spiritually. Their ruling is their heaven; we are in hell. And an Israelite in that hell spends himself teaching the heathen the access he has to our heaven. That is hate. You hate your people and you hate yourself, and for that you are in darkness.

Esau does not forget. He holds grudges: when they took Maduro, rumor has it they bombed the mausoleum where Hugo Chavez is buried, because Chavez spoke ill of America. But Jacob forgets, even in the midst of captivity. The man who says he loves God while caring more for his oppressor than for his own brother is, in John's own word, a liar.

precepts.text: A new commandment: that ye love one another as I have loved you; by this shall all men know ye are my disciples. Repeated in John 15:17.
precepts.point: He that loveth his brother abideth in the light and there is none occasion of stumbling in him; he that hateth his brother walketh in darkness, because that darkness hath blinded his eyes. Hate of your brother blinds you to deep but basic scriptures.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
Where did John get this “new commandment”? From Christ: “A new commandment I give unto you, That ye love one another; as I have loved you, that ye also love one another. By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another.”

Christ said it to the disciples, and John repeated it in his epistle. Christ said it over and over again: “These things I command you, that ye love one another.”

That is why John can say in the same breath, “I write no new commandment unto you, but an old commandment which ye had from the beginning”, and then, “Again, a new commandment I write unto you”. It is old because it came from Moses' time. It is called new because Israel was not following it. Going back to Moses, we were children in whom is no faith, rebellious; we waxed fat and kicked.

So the mark of Christ's disciples is love one to another, among our own people. “He that loveth his brother abideth in the light, and there is none occasion of stumbling in him.” The one who despises his brother and his people will stumble, and stumble in a lot of deep but basic things.

precepts.text: Hear, O Israel, the Lord our God is one Lord; love him with all thy heart, soul, mind and strength; and love thy neighbour as thyself; there is none other commandment greater. Love your people, love your ways.
precepts.point: He that loveth his brother abideth in the light and there is none occasion of stumbling in him; he that hateth his brother walketh in darkness, because that darkness hath blinded his eyes. Hate of your brother blinds you to deep but basic scriptures.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
Normally Matthew 22 is read for this, but Mark is heavy. A scribe asked, “Which is the first commandment of all?” “And Jesus answered him, The first of all the commandments is, Hear, O Israel; The Lord our God is one Lord: And thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind, and with all thy strength: this is the first commandment. And the second is like, namely this, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself. There is none other commandment greater than these.”

There is none greater, because if you love your brother as yourself you can keep all the commandments; they all go hand in hand. You cannot love God and hate your brother. By loving God you will love your brother, and by loving your brother you love God.

What Christ is really saying is: love your people, love your ways. Why would the Most High give us these laws? Because we had learned how to hate one another, and the law was given to teach us. The same laws we give to our people today: love your ways, love your people, love your neighbour.

Think how brainwashed you are in this captivity if, like Deacon Nathan was saying earlier, you are in captivity and care more about your oppressor than your own kind. Your people are being oppressed and all you care about is your oppressor: you're a dummy, and that is the kindest word for it. That is the darkness that “hath blinded his eyes.”

precepts.text: Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart; rebuke thy neighbour; bear no grudge against the children of thy people, but love thy neighbour as thyself. Christ's new commandment was already in the law.
precepts.point: He that loveth his brother abideth in the light and there is none occasion of stumbling in him; he that hateth his brother walketh in darkness, because that darkness hath blinded his eyes. Hate of your brother blinds you to deep but basic scriptures.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
Christ isn't saying anything new. He calls it a new commandment, but we heard it before, in the law: “Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart: thou shalt in any wise rebuke thy neighbour, and not suffer sin upon him. Thou shalt not avenge, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people, but thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself: I am the Lord.”

Your neighbour is your people. Your neighbour is your brother. Love your neighbour as yourself. When you despise yourself, you despise your God that resembles you and your brother that resembles you. It is a domino effect. You can't love one and hate the other.

That is what John means: “Brethren, I write no new commandment unto you, but an old commandment which ye had from the beginning.” It was there from Moses' time. And it is the very hatred Moses warned against in the beginning, when we were all together, that divided Ephraim and Judah. They began to despise each other, and that is why both fell: the northern kingdom first, and the southern kingdom afterward.

So “he that hateth his brother is in darkness, and walketh in darkness, and knoweth not whither he goeth”. Christ's new commandment was already in the law, and Israel's fall came from not keeping it.

precepts.text: Love not the world, neither the things that are in the world.
precepts.point: Friendship with the world is enmity with God, and makes you an adulterer against him.
precepts.why:
“From whence come wars and fightings among you? come they not hence, even of your lusts that war in your members?” It is a consistent battle between the spiritual man and the carnal man. “Ye lust, and have not: ye kill, and desire to have”: you slander the brother or sister who has what you want, give them the evil eye, speak nasty. You ask for a home, a car, a wife, and receive not, because you “ask amiss, that ye may consume it upon your lusts”: to show off, to stunt, to have a trophy wife, to be seen of men.

Christ said if you love the world, you hate me. John writes it: “Love not the world, neither the things that are in the world. If any man love the world, the love of the Father is not in him.” Love not this captivity, neither the precious things and riches in this captivity, neither the mansion on the hill, not even your damn job. A lot of brothers love their jobs more than they love this truth.

These things are hooks inside of you that will pull you out of this truth. They are devices of Satan, the tangible trinkets he gives, which our brothers and sisters lust after as status symbols when the kingdom of heaven is at hand. In Babylon everything is accessible at your fingertips, and everything as far as your eye can see appeals to the flesh.

If any man loves the world, the love of the Father is not in him. That is why James says “the friendship of the world is enmity with God.” Enmity means the state of being actively opposed or hostile, a feud, conflict, bitterness, resentment. That is the mentality that says why do I have to keep the Sabbath, I could be at home, the boxing match is on today. Some sneak off for Christmas and come back with fifteen presents in the trunk. You hate God and God’s laws. This captivity, the dominion of your oppressor, is going to go, and if you don’t kill that old man and that old woman, you are going with him. Kill or be killed.

precepts.text: He that hateth his brother is in darkness and knoweth not whither he goeth, because darkness hath blinded his eyes.
precepts.point: For seven days no leaven is found in the houses; whoever eats that which is leavened, whether stranger or born in the land, is cut off from the congregation of Israel.
precepts.why:
“In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month at even, ye shall eat unleavened bread, until the one and twentieth day of the month at even.” The Passover begins at even and ends at even because the day begins and ends at even. It is not difficult; the scripture says it plainly.

Yet many fell away from the truth over this very point of the day beginning at evening. Sin puts blinders on. “But he that hateth his brother is in darkness, and walketh in darkness, and knoweth not whither he goeth, because that darkness hath blinded his eyes.” When you hate your brother you are in darkness, and darkness blinds the eyes; you cannot see what the scripture plainly says, even something as simple as at even.

So the ones who could not see when the Passover begins were not lacking a verse. They were in darkness, and did not know whither they went.

precepts.text: The propitiation for our sins, the southern kingdom, and also for the sins of the whole world, all twelve tribes of Israel.
precepts.point: That settles 1 John 2:2 for the Christians who run to it. John was a Jew of the southern kingdom, so our sins means the southern kingdom; and not for ours only but also for the sins of the whole world means all twelve tribes, the whole world of Israel. Alongside Isaiah 45:17 and John 18:20, Wisdom of Solomon 18:24 is the precept that shows who the whole world is.

note.label: Exodus 28: Holy Garments for Glory and for Beauty

precepts.why:
“And he is the propitiation for our sins: and not for ours only, but also for the sins of the whole world.” Christians run to this verse, and the breastplate settles it.

John was a Jew of the southern kingdom, so “our sins” means the southern kingdom. “not for ours only, but also for the sins of the whole world” means all twelve tribes, the whole world of Israel: the same whole world the Wisdom of Solomon says was in the long garment, where the four rows of stones carry the names of the twelve tribes.

The whole world in the garment had no Moabite, Jebusite or Edomite stone in it, and neither does the whole world Christ is the propitiation for.

precepts.text: If any man sin, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous, the propitiation for our sins and for the sins of the whole world.
precepts.point: Christ is the advocate and the propitiation, the mercy, for our sins; there is no more Levite priest sacrifice, for he is the mediator between us and the Most High now. The whole world in that verse is the whole world of the nation of Israel.

note.label: Numbers 5: Put Out of the Camp, and the Law of Jealousies

precepts.why:
When a man or woman trespassed against the Lord, they confessed their sin and recompensed it with the principal and the fifth part; and if there was no kinsman, the trespass was recompensed “unto the Lord, even to the priest; beside the ram of the atonement.” The atonement now is Christ. We no longer take a ram to a priest, because Christ became the atonement and we ask forgiveness through him.

“My little children, these things write I unto you, that ye sin not. And if any man sin, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous: And he is the propitiation for our sins: and not for ours only, but also for the sins of the whole world.”

Christ is the advocate and the propitiation, the mercy, for our sins. There is no more Levite priest sacrifice, for he is the mediator between us and the Most High now. The whole world in that verse is the whole world of the nation of Israel.

precepts.text: He that saith, I know him, and keepeth not his commandments, is a liar, and the truth is not in him; the same measure as no light in them.
precepts.point: Thou shalt do that which is right and good in the sight of the Lord: not by personal standards of what feels good in the heart, but by the standard set before us, for the scripture says plainly that the law is good. The reward is to go in and possess the good land, the real wealth, not the bags and rings and sneakers, which are vanity.

note.label: Deuteronomy 6: Teach Them Diligently unto Thy Children

precepts.why:
“He that saith, I know him, and keepeth not his commandments, is a liar, and the truth is not in him.” The same measure as no light in them.

Isaiah says if they speak not according to the law and the testimony there is no light in them; John says if a man keeps not his commandments the truth is not in him. No light, no truth. A personal testimony that cannot come back to the Bible is not biblical, and a man who says he knows him but does not keep the commandments is a liar. Diligently keeping the commandments, testimonies and statutes is how the truth is in you.

precepts.text: The lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, is not of the Father, but is of the world.
precepts.point: This is the same set of temptations the man and the woman met in the garden, and they run through everything the enemy uses.

note.label: Matthew 4: The Temptation in the Wilderness and the Calling of the Fishers

precepts.why:
Christ was led up of the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted, and after fasting forty days and forty nights he was an hungred. The tempter came at the weakest point and went at the flesh first: “command that these stones be made bread.”

John lays out everything the enemy uses: “For all that is in the world, the lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, is not of the Father, but is of the world.” Bread for a hungry man is the lust of the flesh, and that is where the devil began.

This is the same set of temptations the man and the woman met in the garden, and they run through everything the enemy uses: the flesh, the eyes, and pride. “Love not the world, neither the things that are in the world. If any man love the world, the love of the Father is not in him.” Christ, hungry in the wilderness, did not love the world, and so the love of the Father was in him.

precepts.point: Eventually, if you are not of the elect, it will be manifest in your spirit and you will leave. The same thing happened in the apostles' time is happening today under different names but the same spirits.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
The liberty in Christ Jesus is grace and mercy, and the false brethren were able to subvert believers from the gospel and persuade them outside of what they learned. John says the same: “Little children, it is the last time: and as ye have heard that antichrist shall come, even now are there many antichrists; whereby we know that it is the last time.” Antichrist is anybody against the mission or doctrine of Christ.

“They went out from us, but they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would no doubt have continued with us: but they went out, that they might be made manifest that they were not all of us.” They went out from the disciples, from the congregations and churches. Many of the deceivers and heretics come from the body itself, from those who are bitter and hold grudges.

You cannot fake this truth forever. Eventually, if you are not of the elect, it will be manifest in your spirit and you will leave. The same thing that happened in the apostles' time is happening today under different names but the same spirits.

It is the same thing Ezra prophesied: it happened during the time of the apostles and it is happening today. “Little children, it is the last time:” These are the last days. “and as ye have heard that antichrist shall come, even now are there many antichrists;” John said even now there are many antichrists, many people against the Son of God. “whereby we know that it is the last time.” That is how you know these are the last days.

“They went out from us, but they were not of us;” They went out from us, because they were in the midst of sin, and they did videotapes, recordings, to lure out the rest of the simple. That is why God said in Esdras, leave from my sanctuary, and I will not spare you on that day. Who wrote this? The apostle John. When people leave the truth they are not still in the truth. “for if they had been of us, they would no doubt have continued with us:” If they had been of us in this truth they would have still been with us, holding the line. It is us against the world, brothers and sisters: here we are on the battlefield and these men and women leave. They are not of Christ; the Bible says they are antichrist. Don't you realize that the spirit of Christ is about unity? That knucklehead in North Carolina did the same thing: we are on the battlefield and he just jumps up and runs. But they all say, I'm still in the truth. No, you're not. Then he sends links to people in the congregation to watch that abomination; they want men and women to fall out of this truth. They will never say I hate God, I hate Christ; they say I'm against the leadership, they're evil. Who else on this earth is doing the work we are doing? Looking all through YouTube, traveling and looking, it is only us. So you are going to turn from this and go sit in some room with an idiot eating cheese doodles? “but they went out, that they might be made manifest that they were not all of us.” They went out from this truth that they might be made manifest. The deceit is they all say, I'm still in the truth, look, I wear fringes, look how cute me and my family look. They went out that they might be made manifest that they were not all of us. That is the same precept that goes with many are called, but few are chosen.

“The beginning of pride is when one departeth from God”. That's the pride of the world. “and his heart is turned away from his Maker.” Your heart turns away and you want to revel. I've seen young ladies in IUIC with such a worldly look that you can't tell from their pages they're Israelites. It's not so much the drink in their hands; it's the fashion and the whole look. Some leadership turns a blind eye, acts like it doesn't see or care. If this is you, you love the world and still hang with worldly friends. It will be your demise. This isn't in the States; it wouldn't fly in Atlanta, Austin, or New York. You're not coming here with tongue rings. Take that stuff someplace else.

points: “Love not the world, neither the things that are in the world.” Don't have an affinity for or be enamored with its devices. What it offers young men is sin, sexual immorality and sexual deviance. What it offers young women is becoming baby mamas and devaluing yourselves and your bodies. Young people love it because everybody is doing it. Our views are extreme—the polar opposite of the world. It takes fortitude to be an Israelite at school, under peer pressure, and say I don't care what everybody's doing; I'm not joining that. “If any man love the world, the love of the Father is not in him.”

“I have written unto you, fathers, because ye have known him that is from the beginning.” The him is God, the Most High, not your son. The father has known the Most High from when he was young, and now instructs his son not to love the world. That's a leader's instruction to a young man. I was young once; I can relate to where you are. Your greatest gift is listening. You haven't lived enough to understand certain things, even when they make sense to you. Listening saves heartache. If you're already angry about correction, you won't last in this truth; you're going to fall away.

“I have written unto you, young men, because ye are strong”. You can stand on corners teaching for 14 hours; some of us old men can't. “and the word of God abideth in you, and ye have overcome the wicked one.” You must be physically, mentally, spiritually strong. Abide means to house in you. These young ones are going to take over, understand this Bible, and teach it. This is edification, not playing church.

“And this is the promise that he hath promised us, even eternal life.” That's why we do it. If the word abides in you and you don't love the world, you're looking for eternal life. “concerning them that seduce you.” What makes the word leave you? Sin isn't a wrong answer, but seduction is the word. You wouldn't just agree to eat pork, become a whore, or smoke crack. Someone has to seduce you away.

If you're a different person in public school than here or at home, you're seduced. Be the extreme opposite of the world. It doesn't matter what those kids say or do. That little petite guy with a diamond in his forehead—they're pulling you away from the truth. Radicalize your mind instead.

“But the anointing which ye have received of him abideth in you”. Let it abide. “and ye need not that any man teach you”. That doesn't mean nobody teaches you scripture. “but as the same anointing teacheth you of all things”. You don't need the teaching that seduces you away from the Bible. Get away when they start it. They're dimming your light; we're turning it up. Be offensive to this world by your behavior. Again, no guns, no violence. IUIC is a nonviolent movement. We will protect ourselves; that's different. We don't advocate killing anybody of any nation or proclivity. If you're a sodomite, we're not about harming you except with the word of God, and we hope it hurts.

That brother who left was a mouse, petite on the inside, no lion—or a lion with no teeth. Supple, quiet, like a silent and loving woman. They said he once had fire for the work, but he got seduced. Now he says he's been following dumb asses for ten years. Take out dumb; he was following that for twenty years, and I'm talking about men. He wasn't strong, loved the world, couldn't stay off those social media sites or whatever he was doing. Now he talks slick. We know you. You're tender. I pray you repent and leave men's behinds alone. You got some balls, brother. What the hell is wrong with you?

“and even as it hath taught you, ye shall abide in him.” Stay fervent. Not only us, a nation that hasn't woken up yet is counting on you. Young ladies, love yourselves, your name and family. Respect yourselves. That stain is hard, impossible to shake off. For what? You're going to get dragged.

“And now, little children, abide in him”. “and not be ashamed before him at his coming.” Don't be ashamed you're an Israelite, to stand for the word, say you're a virgin, abstain from sex until marriage, or don't celebrate Christmas. To hell with Christmas. To hell with Halloween. Keep your nasty candy. I know peer pressure, but take on this mentality and stand different. We're getting old; you're the generation to keep this going. Don't be a part-time Israelite, sneak behind your parents' backs, or have conversations you shouldn't. Save yourself from this untoward generation.
“every one that doeth righteousness is born of him.” If you do righteousness, you're born of him.
